Grace / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the Calyx document and drafted an initial redline of the MSA sections that typically touch this area (license scope, operator access, termination/forensic access). Key legal points and constraints: 

1) License scope must narrowly define how the runtime may be used in a private deployment — we propose enumerating the permitted runtime operations and add a carve-out for Redwood maintenance tasks that require explicit, auditable customer consent.

2) Operator access: we can commit to "witness/read-only" modes for standard support (no shell or sudo). For higher privilege actions (hotfixes, DB restores) we need:
   - documented change request from customer,
   - mutual time-window, and
   - a two-person authorized process for any elevated action.

3) Escrow alternatives: giving our customers options is reasonable, but each has trade-offs:
   - Sealed snapshot + custodian: acceptable, but we must define the snapshot contents and ensure it excludes Redwood proprietary artifacts (we can provide a sanitized snapshot).
   - KMS/HSM key escrow: acceptable if keys are rotated and handback conditions are limited and auditable; Redwood would require an SLA/indemnity carve-out for misuse after handback.
   - On-site witness: operationally feasible but needs clear scope (what can be witnessed, what evidence is permitted).

4) Audit & evidence: Calyx requests for frequent forensic snapshots and continuous access are a concern. We propose an evidence schedule (quarterly sealed snapshots + on-demand witness with notice) and a defined audit window (e.g., 30 business days to request a witness event from the time of incident).

5) Exhibit proposal: I attached "MSA_Redline_v1.docx" with proposed contract language and an Exhibit B for evidence/escrow options. This is a starting point — legal will need to iterate based on Calyx feedback on snapshot contents and their regulator's expectations.

Ben — please confirm operational constraints/time estimates below so I can mark those as non-negotiables in the redline (e.g., on-site witness prep lead time).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Team / Samir —

Quick tech feasibility + proposed operator-proof workflow options based on the Calyx asks: 

Option A — Sealed snapshot with custodian
- What: periodic sanitized snapshot (VM/image + application config + minimal runtime logs) delivered to an approved custodian (SLA-defined).
- Pros: minimal ongoing access; third party witness is clear.
- Cons: snapshot size, transfer logistics, and the need to define exact sanitization rules to avoid exposing Redwood IP.
- Rough timeline: 2–3 weeks to define snapshot contents and validation process; 1 week for initial custodian handoff.

Option B — KMS/HSM conditional key handback
- What: customer-managed KMS with Redwood holding an encrypted backup of operational keys; under defined triggers Redwood releases the backup following governance checks.
- Pros: cryptographic control, less data transfer than snapshots.
- Cons: complex trigger/attestation workflow; requires coordination on key material handling and indemnity language.
- Timeline: 3–4 weeks for technical runbook and attestation flows.

Option C — On-site witness runbook
- What: Redwood engineer attends a customer site (or on a mutually-approved virtual witness session) to demonstrate operational capability; deliverables include a signed witness log and a check-sum of any artifacts examined.
- Pros: highest confidence for auditors/regulators.
- Cons: scheduling, travel, and clear scope needed; more expensive.
- Timeline: 4–6 weeks minimum (prep, NDAs if required, logistics).

Operational constraints / notes
- For any elevated action we must have a documented change request and the two-person authorization flow Laura noted.
- We can enable a read-only support channel that exposes metrics+logs and a limited console view — no interactive shell.
- We can provide a sanitized, reproducible snapshot recipe (script + validation) so Calyx can validate the snapshot independently.

I've attached a short spreadsheet summarizing these options (Redwood_Escrow_Options_Summary.xlsx). Happy to walk through these items on a call and finalize the proposed Exhibit language with Laura.

— David
